Course of illness:     ******* was born prematurely at 35 weeks gestation as a *******. He was diagnosed with truncus arteriosus at birth[FP32]. He had his first surgical intervention to repair this at the age of 6 weeks. He has had multiple surgical interventions since then. He was undergoing anesthesia for a heart cath back in 2016 when he experienced cardiac arrest. He was then admitted to the ***** for about 10 days after this. He was fine and healthy until about a few weeks ago when Dr. ******* noted changes of left ventricular enlargement that was found on an echocardiogram. He is now admitted to ** ****** ****** for an inpatient heart transplant evaluation.       Family History:     The paternal grandmother had breast cancer. The paternal grandfather died from a heart attack. A maternal nephew was diagnosed with ** ****** syndrome and associated heart conditions. There is no other reported family medical history.     There is no reported mental health history[FP33]. However, mom has admitted in the past that she had anxiety[FP34] around the time of *******'s cardiac arrest in 2016. Mom reported she was taking Zoloft or Prozac when the children were younger and around the same time of her father's passing[FP35].      ******* has an IEP for emotional disturbance at school. His parents stated that he still has difficulty with math and he expresses frustration with this subject. He reports that he continues to struggle with math but that he does like reading. Mom informed SW that she is reading ***** ****** novels to him.      ******* is very shy and reserved. When SW would ask questions he would respond very quietly and would have mom speak up for him or answer for him outright. When asked if he still did not like the 'stickers' that are used for the EKG, he nodded in disapproval.      Mom has a history of alcohol abuse. She states that she has been clean for 7 years[FP36] now and she expresses that she has to do this to be there for her kids. Dad denied any form of substance abuse[FP37]. However, mom privately disclosed to SW after initial assessment that dad has drove while under the influence on several occasions[FP38] with their children[FP39]. She also reports that he smokes marijuana as well[FP40]. There is no other reported history of substance abuse in this family[FP41]. There is no reported history with DCF[FP42]. There is no reported history of domestic violence in the family[FP43].        Adherence:  There are no concerns for adherence noted[FP44]. Mom reports that ******* is okay with taking medications. She states that he has only missed medications once or twice when he has to take them. However, mom is planning on establishing a system for ******* to take his medications. She reports currently using a 7 day/night pill box to schedule his medications. Mom is planning on using an alarm on their phones, especially after transplant, in order to have 100% adherence with medications. Mom verbalized understanding that this will be especially crucial after heart transplant[FP45]. During initial assessment, dad seemed to understand the necessity of taking medication[FP46]. However, mom disclosed privately to SW that she was worried about dad adhering to medication regimen[FP47].      Mom reported being worried about the risks associated with post-transplant[FP48]. When ******* was asked how he felt about transplant, he appeared a little scared. He seemed to be willing to go forward with transplant if this means him feeling better[FP49] and being able to be more physically active, such as being able to swim or running with his siblings[FP50].  Mom and ******* express that if the procedure will allow him to live longer, they are willing to move forward.[FP51]      Assessment and recommendations:     IMPRESSION: Per mom's report, there may be reasons to be concerned for the safety of ******* in his father's care[FP52]. Mom has expressed that dad may be unable to adhere to medication regimens, especially after heart transplant[FP53]. She has also reported reckless behavior on dad's part. She notes that dad has driven under the influence on multiple counts[FP54] with the children in the car and occasions where dad did not express concern for his children[FP55]. If mom is the primary caregiver, it is to be noted that she has limited support[FP56].      Recommendations:  *Provide continuing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care  *Offer support and guidance to mom when needed.   *Assist with identifying additional financial resources and linking mom to them.  *Assist with patient's coping mechanisms in re: to heart transplant  *Identify additional support for mom to help provide care for *******[FP57]     (Low Risk - 1;
